name: Jack Cregan

education.notes: Early education / university not surfaced from public sources reviewed.

keyDecisions: Co-founded Rebills — a payment-orchestration company — as his first founder reps in Irish fintech.
Sold Rebills for $10M in 2024 — a small but clean exit that established him as a 'proven founder' in the Dublin payments scene before Paymend.
lessons: A small clean exit ($10M-scale) in your mid-20s is a credible founder credential — it doesn't have to be a unicorn to earn the next venture's tailwind.
Payment orchestration is a credible Irish fintech sub-niche — Dublin's regulatory access + ACA talent base support it.
careerSteps.notes: Rebills.io acquired in 2024 for $10M per LinkedIn-derived coverage. Co-founder details and exact dates not publicly disclosed.

keyDecisions: Founded Paymend in Dublin post-Rebills exit with co-founder Daniel Harding (COO) — same vertical (payments) but moved up-stack from orchestration to revenue recovery.
Acted as merchant of record and assumed transaction risk — a structurally harder model than pure SaaS that requires real domain credibility.
Stayed bootstrapped (no public VC) — used the Rebills exit proceeds to fund the next venture rather than raising.
Recovered $53M in failed card payments in 2025 with a 25-person team across six countries.
lessons: Bootstrapped second venture funded by a small first-exit is a clean European founder pattern — avoids dilutive capital while you find PMF.
Repeat founder in the same vertical (payments) compounds faster than swap-vertical founder — domain knowledge is the cheaper-to-acquire half.
Acting as merchant of record (taking on risk) is the kind of move only an exited operator with conviction can credibly make.
Geographic spread (6 countries in year one) without raising VC is achievable when the product is a financial-infrastructure layer rather than a brand.
careerSteps.notes: Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2026. Paymend recovered $53M in failed payments in 2025 with 25-person team across 6 countries; bootstrapped.
